about: Eric T. Kirk is a personal injury firm with a single office in Baltimore.
The firm publishes little about cost or availability on the pages we read. It does not state a fee model on its public pages, so none is recorded here.

google.source: Google Business Profile via Places API. 1 listing, counts summed and rating weighted by count

completeness.note: Categories, opening hours, photo count and description come from the Places API. The services list, the Q&A and recent posts are owner-side fields the API does not expose at any price, so they are not scored either way.

ahrefs.source: Ahrefs Site Explorer, batch endpoint, subdomains mode, organic figures for the United States

G1.evidence: Maryland does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

G2.evidence: Maryland does not publish a disciplinary register we can query.

G3.evidence: 1 physical location verified on Google Business Profile. Maryland publishes no business register we can query. SDAT's entity search is a form rather than a dataset, its bulk data is sold rather than published, and the state's open data portal carries a count of businesses instead of the register. This is a limit of the published record and not something the firm can change.

G5.evidence: Site has served over HTTPS, a working phone number published, no attorney is named on the site we could read. The gate also asks for no misleading claims, which is an editorial read we have not recorded.

G6.evidence: 109 public client reviews across 1 Google listing, above the 10 minimum, and the firm's domain has been registered since 2009-04-15, so it has been operating for more than a year
G6.source: Google Places API and the domain's registration date over RDAP

json_ld_descriptions: Not long after receiving his law degree in New York from the oldest independent law school in America in the early 90s, Eric T. Kirk began waging legal warfare against the nation’s largest insurance companies to recover compensation wrongfully withheld from his clients. He’d additionally authored several volumes detailing the 4th, 5th, and 6th Amendment rights of those facing criminal prosecution. Since then, he’s handled thousands of cases in Maryland, New York, and Florida and tried hundreds of cases in various courtrooms throughout Maryland. He has secured millions of dollars in compensation which had been denied or delayed to those in search of a financial award for personal injury. He’s been lead defense counsel in hundreds of criminal prosecutions, guaranteeing, and vindicating the rights of those accused of crime. Mr. Kirk routinely publishes articles and commentary on personal injury and criminal defense topics.
